explanation: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) and flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) are essential coenzymes of oxidation-reduction (redox) reactions in cellular respiration. NAD+ can oxidize a metabolite by accepting electrons or reduce a metabolite by donating electrons. Each NAD+ molecule is highly stable and recycled repeatedly. FAD is another redox coenzyme, used in place of NAD+ in certain metabolic steps. FAD accepts two electrons and two hydrogen ions (H+) to become FADH2.

questions.q: What is the primary role of NAD+ and FAD in cellular respiration?
opts: They act as structural proteins in the mitochondrial outer membrane.
They function as coenzymes of oxidation-reduction, transferring electrons.
They directly hydrolyze ATP to release mechanical energy.
They split glucose into carbon dioxide and water molecules.

questions.q: What does FAD accept to become FADH2?
opts: One electron and one hydrogen ion (H+)
Two electrons and one hydrogen ion (H+)
